variants.name: PartialFunction chain with orElse
variants.idiom_name: PartialFunction[Request, Response] combined with orElse / applyOrElse
variants.implementation_notes: Scala replaces the successor link with `PartialFunction#orElse`: `isDefinedAt` is the 'can I handle this request?' test, `apply` is the handling step, and `auth orElse cache orElse fallback` is the chain evaluated left to right until a function is defined at the input. `applyOrElse` is the efficient evaluation path (a single definedness check per request) and every `case` block already is a partial function, so handlers are ordinary pattern matches rather than classes. Use this instead of a handler hierarchy; keep a real class hierarchy only when handlers need injected collaborators and identity.
variants.code_sketch:
type Handler = PartialFunction[Request, Response]

val chain: Handler = authHandler orElse cacheHandler orElse fallbackHandler

def dispatch(request: Request): Response =
  chain.applyOrElse(request, (_: Request) => Response.unhandled)
pitfalls: orElse is left-biased and calls isDefinedAt on each link, so side effects hidden in guards run even when that handler does not apply.
An exception thrown inside a handler body escapes the chain instead of falling through; wrap handlers in Try when failure must continue the search.
A guard that throws makes isDefinedAt itself unsafe - keep pattern guards pure and total.

variants.name: Play HTTP filter chain
variants.implementation_notes: Inside Play the same pattern arrives as filters: `Filter.apply(nextFilter)(requestHeader)` receives the next link as a function, returns a `Future[Result]`, and may decline to invoke it (blocking the request) or transform the result afterwards. `HttpFilters`/`DefaultHttpFilters` fixes the order and `EssentialFilter` is the lower-level form with access to the request body. Prefer it over hand-rolled chains inside a Play application, where the router and the action are already the terminal link.
pitfalls: Every filter needs an ExecutionContext in scope; a missing implicit fails to compile rather than degrading.
Not invoking nextFilter is a deliberate short-circuit (for example a redirect) but looks like a bug to readers; document it.
Blocking calls inside a filter starve the dispatcher; keep filters asynchronous and delegate to Future combinators.
